rule.description: The pinyin style rendering policy must be owned by one location. The rule enumerates every production function that holds its own conditional pinyin-style decision (an if/switch over the exported style constants or the Args.Style field) and reports the smell when that decision authority is spread over several owner functions or files (>= 2 files or >= 3 owner functions), so that a conceptual change to a style (adding one, or moving one between families) requires coordinated edits across the conversion pipeline. Test files and style references used purely as data (for example lookup-table keys) are not owners. Implemented as a custom go/analysis analyzer (singlechecker driver, golang.org/x/tools v0.17.0) embedded in smell_check.sh.

checks.description: Detects production functions that each own a conditional pinyin-style dispatch, i.e. an if/switch whose guard or case expressions reference the exported style constants (Normal/Tone/Tone2/Tone3/Initials/FirstLetter/Finals/FinalsTone/FinalsTone2/FinalsTone3 and the deprecated aliases) or the Args.Style field, and that select or transform syllable output based on it. The smell is reported when the owners span >= 2 files or >= 3 owner functions.
checks.detected_relation: owner function -> own conditional decision within the shared pinyin style rendering policy
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Before the change this policy lived in exactly one location; after it, deciding how a style renders a syllable requires agreement among several owner functions in four files, so a conceptual change (new style, style redefinition, family regrouping) must be replicated everywhere — the shotgun-surgery signature.

matches.evidence: SinglePinyin (the per-character dictionary/fallback entry) inlines an Initials contraction loop (if a.Style == Initials over the candidate list) before heteronym selection, taking over the whole Initials rendering that the syllable-fixup stage used to own.

applyStyle (the result-collection and heteronym de-duplication loop) now performs its own FirstLetter truncation (if a.Style == FirstLetter) on every collected syllable instead of the syllable-fixup stage doing it.

decodePhoneticSymbol owns the tone-symbol decoding family grouping (switch a.Style: Normal/FirstLetter/Finals strip tone digits; Tone2/FinalsTone2/Tone3/FinalsTone3 keep digit form; default keeps tone marks), moved next to the phoneticSymbol table with the rePhoneticSymbol/reTone2 regexes.

repositionToneNumber in the new tone feature file owns the numeric-tone position decision (switch a.Style over Tone3/FinalsTone3 applying the reTone3 digit move), with the regex relocated from the core.

extractFinals in the new finals feature file owns the finals-family membership (switch a.Style over Finals/FinalsTone/FinalsTone2/FinalsTone3) plus the nasal-syllable special case, co-located with final/handleYW and the j/q/x exception data moved out of the core.

aggregation.report_threshold: >= 2 files carrying conditional style dispatch, or >= 3 owner functions in one file

excluded: Test files (*_test.go) are never counted as owners.

The clean implementation keeps its whole style policy inside one function, so the same rule deliberately does not fire on it: the threshold expresses the one-owner requirement rather than forbidding dispatch outright.

Style constants referenced as data rather than dispatch (e.g. composite-literal keys of a lookup table, the constant declarations themselves, and the cli/pinyin style-flag table in the nested module which is outside the analyzed package) are not owners, so table-driven consolidations remain valid repairs.

toFixed (the thin sequencer over the fragments) carries no conditional style decision of its own and is intentionally not reported; the owners reported above are the ones a conceptual style change would have to touch.
